The plant is added in the companion data center batch (record us-il:new:milkweed-energy-center), so this watch item is closed. The earlier search had read only the public notice feed, which does not list this permit. Earlier notes: Monarch Rock Air, a company tied to Monarch Energy, plans a data center campus on Friday Road in Rockford, Illinois. A Rock River Current article from June 2026, based on state incentive records, says the campus has associated power generation and is a 1,400 megawatt phased data center. That is the size of the data center, not of any power plant. The task list mentions 250 MW of gas engines planned for 2027 from Monarch's own website. I could not confirm that: the Monarch page is built with scripts and showed no text about Illinois or engines, and other articles describe ComEd grid supply. Still unknown: fuel, number of engines, generating capacity and air permit. Check for an Illinois air permit application. If added later, the captive fields are captive industry use power and captive industry type data center.

records.monitor_reason: Prairie Power's Alsey plant in Scott County has six gas turbines that total 169 MW, but no single unit reaches 50 MW. The largest, a GE LM6000 PC Sprint added in 2016, is 48 MW in the EIA-860M table and 45 MW on the owner's own page, though the state air permit calls it nominal 50 MW.
records.researcher_notes: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists plant 7818, Prairie Power Inc, at 331 Campbell Road, Alsey, Scott County, with six operating natural gas turbines of 30, 30, 20, 20, 25 and 48 MW. Five date from 1999 and the sixth from December 2016. Prairie Power's own portfolio page at https://www.ppi.coop/about/assets/ says the plant has six units, five in service since June 1999 and a sixth added in 2017, a simple cycle 45 MW GE LM6000 PC Sprint, for 169 MW in all. Prairie Power's February 15, 2016 release at https://www.ppi.coop/prairie-power-inc-awards-proenergy-services-llc-electric-generation-epc-project/ describes the addition as a 42 MW GE LM6000 PC Sprint and names the older machines as three Westinghouse W251 turbines and two GE LM2500 turbines. The Illinois EPA Clean Air Act permit 01050083 at https://webapps.illinois.gov/EPA/DocumentExplorer/Documents/Index/170000148169?dwdocid=1352176 names the plant and Prairie Power and, in section 4.2, calls the sixth turbine ACT 6, nominal 50 MW at 467 million Btu per hour. How the threshold applies: the three Westinghouse W251 machines are frame turbines and count one per unit, each under 50 MW. The two LM2500 turbines are aeroderivative machines installed together in 1999 and would be one unit of 40 MW. The LM6000 was installed on its own in 2016 and is one unit of 48 MW by the EIA nameplate. So no unit reaches 50 MW and the plant is not added. The LM6000 is a close call. The permit's nominal 50 MW rating would put it at the threshold, while the EIA nameplate of 48 MW, the owner's 45 MW figure and the 42 MW figure in the award release all fall short. The EIA nameplate is used. Check again in a year for any uprate or added unit. The owner, Prairie Power Inc, is already in GEM's company list as entity 100001001384.
